unit.why: A short anecdote: the Apter Rav tells exaggerations at a meal with R. Barukh of Medzhybizh, onlookers wait for mockery, and R. Barukh instead praises his weighed speech.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a series of anecdotes about the Apter's exaggerations told by the Neskhizer; self-contained.

stories.start_quote: וסיפר עוד שפ"א ישב האפטער בסעודה
stories.summary_en: The Apter Rav told exaggerations at a meal with R. Barukh of Medzhybizh; onlookers hoped R. Barukh would laugh, but after the Apter left, R. Barukh praised him as the wisest man in Poland, who weighs every word on a golden scale before speaking.

tags.why: the Apter tells exaggerated tales at a meal, and the whole anecdote is framed as told by the Neskhizer

quotes: ישב האפטער בסעודה עם הרה״ק ר״ר ברוך ממעזיבוז
tags.why: two tzaddikim meet at a meal

quotes: מכל אנשי פולין לא ראיתי חכם כמוהו
tags.why: the apparently laughable exaggerations are revealed as wisdom
illustrates the Apter's wisdom and careful speech

tags.why: onlookers expect R. Barukh, known for sharpness, to mock the other tzaddik
